name: Diana Baldwin
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember whistling a docking tune in an empty yard.” People around the downtown fountain know Diana by a small Sunday habit. Diana keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I still whistle her old docking tune. The successor wrote a different verse for it.
appearance: Diana has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for brown hair pinned away from the temples. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. In conversation Diana rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Diana admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Diana learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To include the successor's verse in the docking song.
family: Jules Brady is Diana’s cousin raised in the same household. Diana leaves the first voice message. Jules calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A closing hour*, Jules says, “I left my grandfather's coat inside Friday night.”
connections: Oakley Carbone. A docking tune gives a child a first pier lesson they can remember at home.

reactions.response: Diana asks what actual work, hours and wage go with the shore title.
